messages:
Ana: Heads-up — between 03:12 and 03:22 UTC we had ~30 node terminations in the spot-gpu pool, lots of immediate pod restarts. k8s events show drain started but pods were re-scheduled onto other spot nodes that then got preempted.
Chris: Oof. Are those from a single region or multiple?
Ana: Mostly us-west1-b. Pattern: termination notice -> node becomes NotReady -> CA scales another spot node in same pool -> new node also gets notice within 2-3m.
autoscaler-bot: [event] cluster-autoscaler: scale-up: triggered for Deployment/rl-training replicas=8 -> added 2 nodes (nodegroup-spot-gpu-3)
Devon: Sounds like correlated preemption window for that GPU SKU in the zone. We should avoid spinning up matching capacity in the exact same spot profile.
Maria: Cost tradeoff though — if we route to on-demand/dedicated we pay a lot. Can we do graded fallback?
Chris: Yes — proposal: mixed-capacity pools with prioritized node groups + drain backoff on spot groups so CA doesn't immediately top up into identical capacity.
Ana: Also saw lots of kube-prober failures where the termination handler tried to drain, but the preStop hook for our driver ddp job hangs for 30s and then kubelet kills it -> no graceful KV flush. That causes longer pod restart churn.
Devon: Two actionable items I can test tomorrow: 1) add an annotation to spot nodegroups to mark "prefer-heterogeneous-provisioning=true" and change CA filters, 2) increase node drain backoff (so CA delays scale-up for Xs after a spot drain).
Maria: Would be good to capture metrics for how often CA immediately replaces nodes vs waits. Might be able to tune cost vs availability.
Chris: Example config change for CA (helm values) I sketched:
```yaml
autoDiscovery:
  clusterName: redwood-prod
  nodeGroupAutoDiscovery: true
filters:
  - name: MixedInstancePolicy
    preferHeterogeneous: true
scaleDown:
  delayAfterAdd: 10m
  unneededTime: 15m
```
Devon: Also add this annotation to spot nodegroups so autoscaler or an admission hook can bias choices: `node-group.redwood.com/provision-hint: avoid-self-correlation`
Ana: For kubelet/drain issues, quick workaround: set `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` on the pods to 120, and add a preStop that triggers async checkpoint then returns quickly. Example:
```yaml
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["/bin/sh","-c","/usr/local/bin/kv-flush & sleep 1"]
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 120
```
Maria: That helps but longer grace on many pods means slower scale-downs. We should only do that for stateful training jobs.
Chris: Agreed. Another lever: node tainting during termination notice window. Flow: watch for GCE/Azure spot signal -> taint node `spot/terminating:NoSchedule` -> controllers see taint and use eviction priorities to move non-critical pods first.
Devon: Right. The lifecycle hook should: on termination notice: 1) annotate node with `spot-interrupt-hint: ts` 2) taint as you said 3) signal drain-backoff by adding `nodegroup.redwood.com/drain-backoff-until: <ts+5m>` so CA won't immediately spawn same flavor.
Ana: Can we implement that with an instance metadata watcher + a small controller? I can throw up a PoC.
Devon: Yep. PoC outline:
```bash
# simple watcher
while true; do
  token=$(curl -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" http://metadata/computeMetadata/v1/instance/preempted)
  if [ "$token" = "TRUE" ]; then
    kubectl taint nodes $NODE spot/terminating:NoSchedule --overwrite
    kubectl annotate node $NODE nodegroup.redwood.com/drain-backoff-until=$(date -d "+5 minutes" --iso-8601=seconds) --overwrite
  fi
  sleep 5
done
```
Maria: We'll need RBAC, but doable. Also confirm CA understands the drain-backoff annotation or we add a small webhook that blocks scale-up into groups whose annotation is active.
Chris: Alternatively, modify the nodegroup scaler lambda that chooses which group to scale — prefer groups without active drain-backoff annotation. Less invasive to CA.
Devon: Good idea. I can add a guard in our provisioning lambda: query nodegroups for `drain-backoff-until` and deprioritize.
Ana: One more item: tune cluster-autoscaler max-graceful-termination for pods with PodDisruptionBudget so CA waits longer before evicting critical pods.
Maria: Let's also add a metric: `spot_pool_replacement_ratio = replaced_nodes / initial_terminated_nodes` and a dashboard for correlation across AZs. I can own that.
Chris: Nice. Quick checklist then: 1) Ana PoC instance watcher (PoC PR) 2) Devon modify provisioning lambda to honor drain-backoff 3) Chris open CA helm tweak RFC for preferHeterogeneous + scale down delays 4) Maria dashboard + cost analysis.
Ana: I'll start the watcher PoC and post a PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Devon: I'll sketch the provisioning change this week.
Maria: I'll wire the metric and estimate cost delta for favoring on-demand fallback per zone.
Chris: Thanks team. If anyone sees the pattern again, paste node names and `kubectl describe node` output here.
Ana: Will do. Quick dump from one node that got notice: `kubectl describe node gpu-spot-23` showed `Taints: spot/terminating:NoSchedule` (added by preempt-handler) and `Annotations: spot-interrupt-hint=2026-07-14T03:13:05Z`
autoscaler-bot: [event] cluster-autoscaler: scale-up activity suppressed for nodegroup-spot-gpu-3 due to drain-backoff annotation (simulated)
Chris: Perfect test signal. We'll iterate.
